readings.distinction: Two contextual interpretations warrant consideration: the factors are jointly necessary, with possible additional legal requirements, or the paragraph presents them as a sufficient trigger within its stated setting. Both yield the same conjunction for the requested antecedent, so they do not justify separate Boolean readings. The universal 'all' attaches to the three listed factors; neither a disjunction nor an independent override based on family-office status is defensible here. The later ordinary-course language qualifies classification as a business, while Q5's 'primarily' cautions against treating this predicate as a complete legal verdict.

readings.subject: Selected control: the three conditions in Family Offices Q3, after any regulated-activity carve-out has been resolved. The requested Boolean is whether the stated licensing trigger is satisfied, not whether the office holds a licence. Retain facts requiring judgment and all qualifications. Controlled text-interpretation study: supplied pages may be experimental variants. Do not infer legal authority from the URL alone.

vocabulary_concerns: The three Boolean inputs encode classification outcomes, not the underlying case facts, Type 9 carve-out criteria, or the defeasible force of 'should not in the ordinary course'. Their adequacy depends on external professional judgment.

The vocabulary cannot distinguish joint necessity from legal sufficiency or encode additional requirements from the incorporated Circular and Ordinance. That unresolved distinction does not change the selected antecedent.

The link between the services, the business providing them, and the location of that same business must be preserved when supplying inputs; the Boolean vocabulary cannot independently verify that linkage.
